Interface JournalFactory

All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultJournalFactory
public interface JournalFactory
Factory for constructing and connecting to Journal instances.

Two creation modes are supported:

  • create — eagerly provisions a new journal in the backend. Performs I/O immediately and throws JournalAlreadyExistsException if a journal with the same name already exists. Name collision is the sole trigger — the inactivity TTL and other arguments passed here are not compared against the pre-existing resource; policy reconciliation is the caller's responsibility.
  • connect — returns a handle to an existing journal without performing backend I/O at factory call time. The first read, append, or subscribe operation on the handle probes the backend once: if no journal exists at name, that first operation throws JournalNotFoundException. Journal.delete() does not probe and remains a retry-safe no-op when the journal is already gone. Once the one-shot probe passes, subsequent operations behave exactly as they would on a create-sourced handle — terminal-state transitions surface as JournalExpiredException or JournalCompletedException in the normal way.

  • Method Details

    • create

      <T> Journal<T> create(String name, Class<T> type, Duration inactivityTtl)
      Creates a new journal with the given name and inactivity TTL.

      This method performs backend I/O immediately to provision the journal. Name collision is the sole trigger for JournalAlreadyExistsException — the inactivityTtl passed here is not compared against any pre-existing journal's configuration; policy reconciliation is the caller's responsibility.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the entry payload type
      Parameters:
      name - the unique name for the journal
      type - the payload class
      inactivityTtl - how long the journal lives without appends before auto-expiring; must be strictly positive
      Returns:
      a new Journal instance
      Throws:
      JournalAlreadyExistsException - if a journal with the given name already exists
      IllegalArgumentException - if inactivityTtl is zero or negative, or exceeds the maximum allowed duration

    • create

      <T> Journal<T> connect(String name, Class<T> type)
      Connects to an existing journal by name.

      No backend I/O is performed at factory call time. The first read, append, or subscribe operation on the returned handle probes the backend once and throws JournalNotFoundException if no journal exists at name. Journal.delete() does not probe and remains a retry-safe no-op. Once the one-shot probe passes, the handle behaves exactly as one returned from create — subsequent terminal-state transitions surface as JournalExpiredException or JournalCompletedException.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the entry payload type
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the journal to connect to
      type - the payload class
      Returns:
      a Journal handle
      Throws:
      JournalNotFoundException - at first operation, if no journal exists at name (surfaced on the first read/append/subscribe call, not at connect time)
